details: Found by the review of the test-token fix (30 Oct): the fix covers tests/run_unittest.py, but pytest on a machine without relay still creates and leaves $HOME/.relay/test-tokens, the same leak seen on the VPS ai.amidman.com. Its twin finding F4 (relay_ledger binds ledger_dir at import) is item a-test-leaves-relay-ledger-bound-to-a-patched-le.
failing_case: HOME=<empty scratch folder>, RELAY_HOME and RELAY_TEST_TOKENS unset:
`pytest -q tests/test_relay_tokens.py -k 'test_defaults or RunnerPool'` -> 5 passed, and afterwards
<HOME>/.relay/test-tokens/token-8 and <HOME>/.relay/test-tokens/waiting exist. Expected: HOME left empty.
pass_cases: 1. Empty HOME, RELAY_HOME unset: after a pytest run HOME is empty.
2. Under relay gate (RELAY_TEST_TOKENS passed), the pytest session still uses the gate's pool and takes no token.
3. On a machine whose pool exists, a pytest session still takes one SHARED token of it.
reason: tests/test_pytest_pool_home.py::test_empty_home_stays_empty passes on head, fails at f7d7626 without the fix.

details: CONFIRMED by mutation. The test asserts only that HOME stays empty and that P/test-tokens was not created. A conftest
that ignores the passed-down base also leaves both untouched: it makes a temporary pool, takes a token there, and
removes it. So the brief's pass case 2 ("still uses the gate's pool and takes no token") has no test that tells the
two apart. The behaviour itself is correct today (own_pool_home returns run_home when passed_down is non-zero, and
its own tests in test_relay_tokens.py cover that), so this is a weak test, not wrong code. Size: 15 minutes.
failing_case: Change tests/conftest.py pytest_sessionstart to always use a temporary pool
Now: test_gate_pool_is_used_and_no_token_taken still passes (only test_existing_pool_is_used fails).
Expected: the gate-pool test fails, since the session took a token instead of using the base the gate passed down.
fix_hint: Make the child show what it saw: e.g. let the pytest child print os.environ RELAY_TEST_TOKENS from a session hook
(or run a tiny test via -p with a plugin that writes it to a file) and assert it equals the hold the gate passed;
or test pytest_sessionstart directly with a monkeypatched environment and assert _session_base[0].passed is True
pass_cases: 1. RELAY_HOME=P, RELAY_TEST_TOKENS=hold_value(2, P), P/test-tokens absent: the session's base is passed down
(base.passed is True, workers 2), no temporary pool is made, and RELAY_TEST_TOKENS is left as the gate gave it.
2. Same, with the conftest mutated to always use a temporary pool: the test fails.
3. Empty HOME, RELAY_HOME and RELAY_TEST_TOKENS unset: HOME stays empty (test_empty_home_stays_empty, unchanged).
4. RELAY_HOME=P with P/test-tokens existing: a token-N file appears in P/test-tokens (test_existing_pool_is_used, unchanged).
reason: tests/test_pytest_pool_home.py: gate-pool test now uses a spy plugin asserting passed, workers, no temp homes; it passes on head and fails on base (module has no _session_temp_homes).
findings.summary: test_gate_pool_is_used_and_no_token_taken passes when the conftest ignores the gate's pool and takes a token of a temporary one
